chapter: Kline 1980: early years and founding of the Goldkette orchestra
title: Goldkette's business role and the Horvath family
summary: Virginia explains that her father Steven and brother Charlie worked with Goldkette, a classically trained musician who handled the business side of the Detroit orchestra.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Jean Goldkette was playing at the DAC in Detroit, which is the Detroit Athletic Club. And he had quite a name for himself. And the association with my father and brother.

Jean was already known in Detroit and they were getting this band together to open up the Graystone Ballroom. They decided to use Jean's name because he was well known. Now Jean didn't have to lead the band. But he, being a classical musician, just was not cut out too well. Actually he tried very hard but he just couldn't do it. And so that he and my brother worked together, we did the bookings and things like that. And Jean Goldkette was - well I don't know, he was mostly name. He never led the band.
And he wasn't that concerned I guess with the arrangements?
Because he was really on the business side.
He was really on the business side.
Yeah, he was on the business side.
He was strictly a classical man.
How can a man with that background know that much about jazz? He loved jazz, didn't he?
But he had a feel for it apparently.
